text: Ten fictional nonprofit passages in varied genres, each with eight citation test variants.

passages.source_passage: Since the October board meeting, the Dryland Seeds Collective has distributed sorghum and cowpea seed to 1,420 households across the Karamba plateau. Field staff reported that 68% of plots were sown within a week of the first rains. Rainfall in March was not sufficient for the late maize trial, so we did not extend it beyond the original 12 demonstration farms. No farmer has withdrawn from the programme, and four farmer groups have asked to host training days in 2025. The next review is planned for June, when we will compare yields against last season's baseline.

passages.source_passage: In this session, volunteers learn to measure a child's mid-upper arm circumference and to record the result on the green household card. Each volunteer in the Mbala District Health Programme visits about 25 households every month, and refers any child with a red reading to the clinic within 48 hours. Do not give medicine yourself, because only the clinic can decide on treatment. You are not expected to diagnose illness, and you should never promise a family that treatment will be free unless the clinic has confirmed it. Since 2022, more than 300 volunteers have completed this module, and about nine in ten now record readings correctly.

passages.source_passage: The Riverbend Food Security Fund completed its third cash transfer round in November, reaching 2,310 households with an average payment of 45 dollars. A post-distribution survey found that 72% of recipients bought staple food first, while fewer than 5% reported spending on alcohol or tobacco. Mobile payment delays were not resolved in the northern wards, and about 140 households received their money more than two weeks late. The finance committee has not approved an increase in the transfer value for next year. Staff will return to the board in February with a revised delivery plan.

passages.source_passage: Between January and September the Lantern Access Project fitted 386 wheelchairs and 214 hearing aids, which is 91% of the annual target. Six of the eight community centres now have step-free entrances. The ramp at Marsh Road Library is unfinished because the municipality has not issued a building permit. No completion date has been confirmed. Users told us the repair workshop is useful, but waiting times average 19 days. Our fiscal year ends on 31 March, and we plan to hold a user feedback forum before then.

passages.source_passage: In the Tamsin Valley, there is one practising lawyer for every 28,000 residents, and most people cannot afford private fees. Since 2019 the Open Door Paralegal Service has held monthly clinics in 17 villages, advising more than 4,600 clients on land, family and employment disputes. Paralegals are not lawyers and do not appear in court, but they help clients prepare documents and negotiate with local officials. An independent review in 2023 found that 58% of land cases were settled without litigation. Women made up only 31% of clients, and the service has not reached the remote hill settlements.

passages.source_passage: Nearly 60% of children in the Sunrise Hills settlements have no access to any form of organised early learning before they start primary school at age six. The Little Steps Playgroup Network, founded in 2016, now supports 48 volunteer-run playgroups that meet three mornings a week. Facilitators are not paid teachers, and the playgroups do not charge fees. A 2022 baseline assessment showed that children who attended for at least a year scored 14 points higher on a language screening tool than their peers. Caregivers also said they were reading to their children more often. However, the network has not collected a formal measure of parenting practice.

passages.source_passage: Before each home visit, check that your bag contains gloves, soap, a thermometer and 7 days of adherence cards. Greet the family and ask permission to come in. Never discuss a client's HIV status with neighbours, even if they ask directly, and do not leave medicine or records where others can see them. During the first month, each volunteer in the Kiwanda Home Care Programme visits every client twice a week; after that, most clients are seen once every 14 days. If a client has missed two doses in a row, call your supervisor the same day.

passages.source_passage: In Dorrel District, only 34% of rural households use a protected water source, and women and girls walk an average of 2.5 kilometres each day to collect water. The Clearwater Village Trust has drilled 22 boreholes since 2018, yet five were not functioning in the last dry season because spare parts were unavailable locally. No village in the district is yet certified open-defecation-free. Latrine coverage rose from 21% to 49% in the programme's target communities, but handwashing facilities were not installed at most household latrines. This proposal seeks funding for 15 further boreholes and a spare-parts supply chain.

passages.source_passage: At the mid-point of the 36-month Bright Dawn Outreach Project, skilled birth attendance in the 40 target villages rose from 52% to 71%. Evaluators found that outreach clinics held on fixed days were well attended, but the referral transport scheme did not meet demand, and 23 women reported waiting more than three hours for a vehicle. The project has not trained enough female community mobilisers to cover the remote upper valleys. Newborn checks within 48 hours of birth were recorded for 64% of deliveries. We recommend that the budget be reviewed before December 2025.

passages.source_passage: In the highland municipalities of Sierra Ixmal, only 38% of girls who finish primary school enrol in secondary school, and fewer than one in five complete it. Families cite the cost of uniforms, transport and fees, and many girls are not able to attend because of long journeys. The Futuro Claro scholarship programme has supported 520 girls since 2017. It does not select students on test scores alone; staff also consider household income and distance from school. Of the 2021 cohort, 83% graduated on time, and none of the scholarship holders married before turning eighteen.
